text: Zero is the only number that can't be represented in Roman numerals. The Romans had no symbol for nothing!
A pizza is a real-life fraction! When you cut it into 8 equal slices and eat 3, you've eaten 3/8 of the pizza.
The word 'mathematics' comes from the Greek word 'mathema', meaning 'knowledge' or 'learning'.
A googol is the number 1 followed by 100 zeros. It's bigger than the number of atoms in the observable universe!
Honeybees build their honeycombs in perfect hexagons. This shape uses the least amount of wax to store the most honey — nature loves efficient geometry!
If you fold a piece of paper in half 42 times, the stack would reach from Earth to the Moon!
The number 12 is called a 'highly composite number' because it has more divisors than any smaller number: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 12.
In ancient Egypt, fractions always had 1 as the numerator (like 1/2, 1/3, 1/5). They would write 3/4 as 1/2 + 1/4!
A century is 100 years, a millennium is 1,000 years, and a megayear is 1,000,000 years. Geologists use megayears to measure Earth's history!
The Fibonacci sequence (1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13…) appears in sunflower seeds, pinecones, and even the spiral of a galaxy.
Multiplication is just fast addition! 6 × 4 means adding 6 four times: 6+6+6+6 = 24.
The symbol % means 'per hundred'. So 35% simply means 35 out of every 100.
A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself. The number 2 is the only even prime number!
The Arabic numeral system (0–9) that we use today was actually invented in India over 1,500 years ago!
Pi (π) is approximately 3.14159… and its digits go on forever without repeating. Mathematicians have calculated over 100 trillion digits of pi!
Doubling a number is the same as multiplying by 2. If you keep doubling from 1, after just 20 doublings you pass 1 million!
The equals sign (=) was invented by Welsh mathematician Robert Recorde in 1557. He chose two parallel lines because 'no two things can be more equal'.
A negative number below zero can describe real things — like temperatures in winter, floors below ground in a building, or a bank account that's overdrawn.
Rounding makes mental math much easier. 198 + 203 is tricky, but 200 + 200 = 400 is instant — then you adjust by −2 + 3 = +1, so the answer is 401!
The tallest building in the world, Burj Khalifa in Dubai, is 828 metres tall. If you rounded that to the nearest 100, you'd say it's about 800 metres.
Skip counting by 2s gives you all the even numbers. Every even number can be split into two equal groups — that's what 'even' means!
A ratio compares two quantities. In a class with 12 girls and 8 boys, the ratio of girls to boys is 12:8, which simplifies to 3:2.
The word 'decimal' comes from the Latin 'decimus', meaning tenth. Every decimal place is a tenth of the one before it.
Ancient Babylonians used a number system based on 60 — that's why we have 60 seconds in a minute and 60 minutes in an hour!
Multiplying any number by 9 has a cool trick: the digits of the answer always add up to 9. Try 9×7=63, and 6+3=9!
A square number is a number multiplied by itself. 4, 9, 16, 25, 36… they form a beautiful pattern on a times table grid.
The fastest mental math trick for multiplying by 5: multiply by 10 first, then halve the result. 5×18 = half of 180 = 90!
Algebra uses letters to stand for unknown numbers — just like a mystery box. Solving x + 5 = 12 means asking: what number plus 5 equals 12?
Division is the opposite of multiplication. If 4 × 6 = 24, then 24 ÷ 6 = 4. Learning one fact gives you two!
The percentage 100% means the whole thing. 50% is half, 25% is a quarter, and 1% is one hundredth of the whole.
The number 1,000,000 (one million) written out in seconds is about 11.5 days. One billion seconds is over 31 years!
Symmetry is everywhere in nature. A butterfly's wings, a starfish, and a snowflake all have lines of symmetry.
To find 10% of any number, simply move the decimal point one place to the left. 10% of 350 is 35.0!
Odd numbers always end in 1, 3, 5, 7, or 9. Even numbers always end in 0, 2, 4, 6, or 8. No exceptions!
The area model shows multiplication as a rectangle. 23 × 14 becomes a rectangle split into smaller parts: 20×10 + 20×4 + 3×10 + 3×4.
A magic square has numbers arranged so every row, column, and diagonal adds up to the same total. The oldest known magic square is from China, over 4,000 years old!
Subtracting is like climbing down a ladder. If you're on rung 15 and go down 7, you land on rung 8. 15 − 7 = 8.
Every fraction can be written as a decimal. 1/4 = 0.25, 1/2 = 0.5, 3/4 = 0.75. They're just different ways to write the same number!
The world uses the metric system for measurement — metres, kilograms, litres. It's all based on powers of 10, making conversion a matter of moving the decimal point.
There are 86,400 seconds in a day. That's 60 × 60 × 24. Every day is a multiplication problem!
A ratio of 1:1 means equal amounts of two things. A 2:1 ratio means twice as much of the first thing as the second.
The Vedic method of multiplication is over 2,500 years old, from ancient India. It uses cross-multiplication patterns that can multiply faster than a calculator!
The number line goes on forever in both directions. Negative numbers go left, positive numbers go right, and zero sits right in the middle.
Counting on your fingers isn't just for babies! Even professional mathematicians use physical objects to think through tricky problems.
The LCM (Lowest Common Multiple) of two numbers is the smallest number both divide into evenly. It's used when adding fractions with different denominators!
Scientific notation is a short way to write very big or very small numbers. The mass of Earth is 5.97 × 10²⁴ kg — much easier than writing 26 zeros!
To multiply a number by 11, add its two digits together and place the sum in the middle. 11 × 36: 3+6=9, so the answer is 396!
The word 'percent' literally means 'per hundred' in Latin. Discounts, exam scores, and bank interest are all measured in percentages.
Every whole number is a fraction! 7 is the same as 7/1. Fractions are just a way of showing division.
The number 0 was a revolutionary invention. For thousands of years humans did maths without it. Ancient Greeks and Romans had no symbol for zero at all!
Skip counting by 3s gives you the 3 times table. If the digits of a number add up to a multiple of 3, that number is divisible by 3!
Maths is the only language shared by all people in the world. 2 + 2 = 4 in every country, every culture, and every century.
